sources.title: Media Fragments URI 1.0 (basic)
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, Media Fragments URI 1.0 (2012)
sources.observed_operation: Web search and direct open of W3C TR
sources.governing_condition_or_default_or_except: Temporal selector t=begin,end uses seconds/NPT by default; bounds are half-open [begin,end); omitted start defaults to 0 and omitted end to source duration. Empty/reversed ranges are invalid.
sources.applicability: Defines interoperable temporal-target syntax and a useful interval convention for exports. It does not define stable recording identity, sample accuracy, UI behavior, or replacement remapping.

sources.title: Web Annotation Data Model
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation (2017); status states stable Recommendation
sources.locator: §1 lines 87–100 (data model/transport); §4.2.1 lines 805–850 (FragmentSelector); §4.2.4–4.2.5 lines 930–993 (text quote/position selectors); §4.3.1 lines 1199–1205 (TimeState)
sources.observed_operation: Web search, direct open, and find within W3C TR
sources.governing_condition_or_default_or_except: A FragmentSelector has a value plus a conformsTo reference. The model is a serialization/data model and does not prescribe a transport protocol. TextPositionSelector is brittle when source text changes; a State is recommended to identify the correct representation.
sources.applicability: Supports an optional local JSON-LD interoperability export and optional transcript text anchoring. It does not by itself identify the exact local recording bytes or justify deriving media timestamps from untimed transcript text.

sources.title: HTML Standard: media elements
sources.version_or_commit: WHATWG Living Standard; snapshot accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: §4.8.11.6 lines 1798–1859 (duration/currentTime/timeline); §4.8.11.9 lines 2401–2479 (seekable, fastSeek, seeking algorithm)
sources.observed_operation: Direct open and find in the WHATWG standard
sources.governing_condition_or_default_or_except: duration is seconds, NaN when unavailable and Infinity for unbounded streams. currentTime is seconds on the resource's media timeline; setting it seeks. fastSeek trades precision for speed. Seeking clamps to source bounds and, when outside seekable ranges, chooses a nearest seekable point; seeking is asynchronous.
sources.applicability: A concrete example of why player adapters must report readiness/seek completion and actual position, and why time precision must not be inferred from decimal formatting. Local recordings normally have finite durations, but player/media metadata still governs actual seek results.
